The Lab Book organizes work around a lifecycle:

`plan -> acquire -> organize -> analyze -> validate -> collaborate -> communicate -> preserve`

Stages overlap and may repeat. A revised project plan can trigger new acquisition work; an intake discrepancy can require a scope decision. Each page distinguishes the **Draft minimum**, **Conditionally required**, **Recommended**, **Stronger practice**, **Example**, and **Stop and resolve** levels.

**Plan**, **Acquire**, **Organize**, and **Analyze** now have implemented draft guidance. Validate, Collaborate, Communicate, and Preserve remain future lifecycle stages, not complete guidance.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  plan[Plan] --> acquire[Acquire]
  acquire --> organize[Organize]
  organize --> analyze[Analyze]
  analyze --> validate[Validate]
  validate --> collaborate[Collaborate]
  collaborate --> communicate[Communicate]
  communicate --> preserve[Preserve]
  acquire -. revise .-> plan
  validate -. revise .-> plan
```

## Choose a starting point

- [Starting a new project](../start/new-project.qmd) for a short gateway and initiation checklist.
- [Plan a project](plan/index.qmd) when purpose, scope, roles, outputs, or completion criteria are unsettled.
- [Plan data management](plan/data-management-planning.qmd) when access, storage, restrictions, identifiers, time, space, or computing need decisions.
- [Receive a one-time dataset](acquire/data-intake.qmd) when a file, archive, extract, sequence batch, raster, or field export arrives.
- [Design recurring or programmatic acquisition](acquire/recurring-programmatic-data.qmd) for APIs, databases, feeds, portals, and scheduled extracts.
- [Assess intake acceptance](acquire/data-intake.qmd#intake-completion-gate) when deciding whether incoming data can enter the Organize stage.
- [Organize accepted data](organize/index.qmd) when a snapshot has passed intake and needs controlled structure, provenance, schema, identifier, spatial, temporal, and readiness checks.
- [Review analysis readiness](organize/index.qmd#analysis-readiness-gate) before allowing a structurally documented dataset to enter Analyze.
- [Design an analysis](analyze/analysis-design.qmd) when the question, target, data version, method, and intended outputs need to be made explicit.
- [Distinguish exploratory and planned work](analyze/exploratory-and-planned-analysis.qmd) when decisions may have changed after seeing results.
- [Record an analysis execution](analyze/computational-execution.qmd) for local, notebook, scheduled, or HPC work.
- [Trace a result](analyze/results-and-traceability.qmd) when an estimate, figure, map, forecast, table, or simulation summary matters beyond a temporary exploration.

The Lab Book separates draft policy, task guidance, templates, and examples. The [Minimum GeoEpi Project Standard](../start/minimum-standard.qmd) supplies the governing draft framework; these pages explain how to satisfy relevant information requirements without prescribing one folder tree, storage platform, workflow engine, or environment.
